Counsel for Applicant :- Yogeshwar Sharan Srivastava Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1.
Heard learned Counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the record.
2. Rejoinder affidavit is taken on record.

3. The applicant has applied for grant of bail for the offence allegedly levelled against him in Case Crime No.10 of 2023, under Section 2/3 of the U.P. Gangsters and Anti Social (Prevention) Act,
Police Station Vikas Nagar, District Lucknow.

entities.text: U.P. Gangsters and Anti Social (Prevention) Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
4. Learned counsel for the applicant argued that in the gang chart, which is on record, two cases were shown against the applicant bearing Case Crime No.0047 of 2021, under Sections 406,420,
467, 468, 471 I.P.C., Police Station Vikas Nagar, District Lucknow and the other case bearing Case Vivek Tripathi vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko. on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10255572/
1 Crime No.0049 of 2021 under the similar sections.

entities.label: ORG

entities.text: Case Vivek Tripathi vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Based upon the said two cases, in terms of the mandate of provisions of U.P. Gangsters Act and the rules framed thereunder, a view was formed to invoke Gangsters Act against the applicant as there was a disturbance of public order and a fear was there in the entire public and because of the said fear, no one was ready to give evidence against the applicant.
5. Per contra, learned A.G.A. has opposed the bail prayer of the applicant.

A counter affidavit was filed by the respondent State arguing that apart from the said two cases referred in the gang chart,
there are as many as 25 cases against the applicant as disclosed in the counter affidavit.

6. Learned A.G.A. is also placed reliance on the mandate of Section 19 (4) of the Gangsters Act to argue that it is the court which is to be satisfied that there are reasonable grounds for believing that the applicant is not guilty of such offence and that the applicant is not likely to commit any offence while on bail.
7. Learned counsel for the applicant in rebuttal to the counter affidavit, stated that in all the cases apart from the two cases shown in the gang chart, the applicant is on bail.
He thus argued that the applicant should be released on bail.

8. In support of his submissions, learned counsel for the applicant placed reliance on the judgement and order dated 3.11.2023 passed by this court in Crl. Misc. Bail Application No.42050 of 2023 :
Angad Rai @ Jhullan Rai Vs. State of U.P.
9.

entities.text: Crl. Misc. Bail Application No.42050 of 2023
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

entities.text: Angad Rai @ Jhullan Rai Vs. State of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Considering the said submissions, prima facie it appears that in the gang chart which has lead to filing of an F.I.R. under the Gangsters Act, only two cases are shown and based upon the said two cases, a view has been formed that on account of the said two cases, there is a threat to public order.

10. This court in the order passed in the case of Angad Rai @ Jhullan Rai (supra) had given its opinion to deal with the definition of 'gang' as defined under Section 2(b) of the Act and after placing reliance o the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Banka Sneha Sheela Vs.
State of Telangana and others : (2021) 9 SCC 415 where the Hon'ble Supreme Court had laid down the distinction between the 'land and order', 'public order' and 'security of the State'.
11. Relying on the said order and reasoning contained therein, the facts of the present case have to be evaluated.

entities.text:
Banka Sneha Sheela Vs.
State of Telangana and others : (2021) 9 SCC 415
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the present case, in two cases shown in the gang chart, both relate to the alleged offence under Sections 406,420, 467, 468, 471 I.P.C.. at the instance of the private persons who had alleged that the applicant was introduced by claiming himself to be a salesman of a company which he was not and certain money was taken by him by misrepresenting the name of the company in which the applicant had worked.
12. While considering the bail order, this Court had in detail, considered the allegations against the applicant which are contained in Annexure No.5.
From perusal of the said two documents, prima facie a view could not be found with regard to disturbance of public order and in the worst case, it could be considered as a problem of law and order.

2 13.
Thus, following the reasoning contained in order dated 3.11.2023 passed in the case of Angad Rai's case (supra), a case for grant of bail is made out.
14. Accordingly, the present application is allowed.

15. Let the applicant Vivek Tripathi be released on bail in Case Crime/ FIR No.10 of 2023, under Sections 2/3 of U.P. Gangsters and Anti-Social Activities (Prevention) Act, 1986 registered at Police Station Vikas Nagar, District Lucknow on his furnishing a personal bond with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of court concerned with the following conditions: -
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
Order Date :- 17.1.2024 Shukla  Vivek Tripathi vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko.
